Fr8Labs Design System

The shared UI foundation for consistent, accessible, and audit-friendly freight workflows.

What FDS provides

Reusable decisions for freight products

FDS packages repeated interface decisions so product teams can assemble workflows without rebuilding controls, states, or interaction rules.

Foundations
Shared tokens and visual rules
Components
Reusable interface controls
Patterns
Approved workflow compositions

Working method

Adopt from the workflow outward

  1. 01Start with the workflow

    Define the task, user role, real freight content, and required states.

  2. 02Assemble approved parts

    Combine the documented parts that support the task.

  3. 03Validate in product

    Test responsive layout, keyboard paths, accessible names, and workflow meaning before release.

getting-started-mcp-pilot--docs.content:
import {Meta, Source} from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import './Welcome.css';

Fr8Labs Design System

MCP pilot

Test whether an AI assistant can find and apply approved FDS guidance. MCP provides read-only catalog access; it does not install the package or modify product code.

Use the shared pilot

Use the hosted endpoint to test the published FDS catalog and Storybook documentation. No repository clone or local server is required.

Run current source locally

Use http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp when validating source changes before deployment.

Configure the MCP client

Restart the client after adding the server. Use the local URL instead when testing source changes; both endpoints expose the same nine read-only tools.

Available tools

search_catalog
Find approved records by query, kind, or FDS version.
get_component
Return an approved component API, dependencies, states, accessibility constraints, and code snapshot.
get_template
Return an approved fake-data template, allowed composition, accessibility constraints, and code snapshot.
get_prompt
Return an approved bounded prompt and its fake-data restriction without running it.
get_token_reference
Resolve an approved token to its CSS variable, alias, and permitted use.
get_adoption_recipe
Return versioned package or owned-copy instructions and the related drift warning.
list-all-documentation
List the IDs for every published Storybook component, pattern, foundation, document, and story.
get-documentation
Return the API, props, guidance, and example stories for one Storybook entry.
get-documentation-for-story
Return the usage example for one published story scenario.

Run the pilot

  1. Ask: “List all FDS Storybook documentation and include story IDs.”
  2. Ask: “Get the documentation for components-actions-button and use its real props and examples.”
  3. Ask: “Get the approved Button catalog record and package adoption recipe.”
  4. Confirm the recipe matches the FDS installation guide.
  5. Use the returned guidance in a disposable Vite application and verify that the sample compiles and renders.

Use synthetic data only. Do not send customer, shipment, invoice, credential, or production data through the pilot.

Report the result

Record the MCP client, prompts, returned FDS version and item IDs, and final outcome. Include any guidance that was missing, confusing, or incorrect.

Fr8Labs Design System

Contributing

Keep reusable decisions in FDS and feature-specific work in the product that owns the workflow.

Choose the right home

  • Reuse an existing component or pattern before adding another one.
  • Put reusable components, tokens, and interaction rules in FDS.
  • Put feature-specific concrete prototypes in the prototyping project.
  • Treat sandbox work as exploration until it is explicitly approved.

Use the Storybook hierarchy

  • Components/<Category>/<Component>
  • Patterns/<Workflow category>/<Pattern>
  • Foundations/<Foundation>
  • Internal/<Purpose>/<Check>

Name story exports after the scenario, state, or decision they demonstrate.

Verify before review

Passing checks confirms implementation quality; reusable design still requires explicit review and approval.
